_notes: Real, verifiable exam bodies mapped to CEFR (or nearest national equivalent). Levels use CEFR A1-C2 where the language has an official CEFR-aligned exam; ILR/ACTFL-style ladders are noted where CEFR doesn't apply. Populate 'skills_tested' and 'level_thresholds' per exam from the official handbook before shipping — these are structurally correct but exact passing scores/dates should be pulled from the exam body's current syllabus at content-build time, since they do change.

exams.name: IELTS Academic
exams.format: Listening 30min, Reading 60min, Writing 60min (2 tasks), Speaking 11-14min (face-to-face or AI-proctored)
exams.scoring: Band 1-9 in 0.5 increments per section, averaged for overall band

exams.name: TOEFL iBT
exams.format: Reading ~35min, Listening ~36min, Speaking 16min, Writing 29min, all on computer
exams.scoring: 0-30 per section, 0-120 total

exams.name: Cambridge English Qualifications (B1 Preliminary / B2 First / C1 Advanced / C2 Proficiency)
exams.format: Varies by level; fixed CEFR-level exam rather than adaptive score like IELTS/TOEFL
exams.scoring: Cambridge English Scale 80-230, pass/fail per fixed level

exams.name: DELF (A1-B2)
exams.body: France Education International / French Ministry of Education
exams.format: Four independent diplomas, one per CEFR level A1-B2, each with 4 sections
exams.scoring: Pass at 50/100 with no section below 5/25

exams.name: DALF (C1-C2)
exams.format: Advanced diplomas, C1 and C2, includes document synthesis task
exams.scoring: Pass at 50/100 with no section below 5/25

exams.name: TCF (Test de Connaissance du Français)
exams.format: Modular; mandatory sections + optional speaking/writing, often required for immigration/university
exams.scoring: Scaled score 100-699 mapped to CEFR A1-C2

exams.name: Goethe-Zertifikat (A1-C2)
exams.format: Level-specific fixed exams, widely required for German visas/citizenship
exams.scoring: Pass at 60/100, per-level

exams.name: TestDaF
exams.format: University-entrance oriented, computer or paper based
exams.scoring: TDN 3-5 per section (roughly B2.1-C1.2)

exams.name: DELE (A1-C2)
exams.format: Fixed level diplomas, official for Spanish citizenship/residency
exams.scoring: Pass at 60% combined, no group below 50%

exams.name: SIELE
exams.body: Instituto Cervantes / Universidad de Salamanca / UNAM / Universidad de Buenos Aires
exams.format: Computer-based, modular, results in days rather than weeks
exams.scoring: 0-1000 scaled score mapped to CEFR A1-C1

exams.name: CILS
exams.format: Fixed CEFR-level exams
exams.scoring: Pass per level, section minimums apply

exams.name: CELI
exams.format: Fixed CEFR-level exams
exams.scoring: Pass per level

exams.name: PLIDA
exams.format: Fixed CEFR-level exams, used for citizenship
exams.scoring: Pass per level

exams.name: CAPLE
exams.format: Fixed CEFR-level exams (Portugal)
exams.scoring: Pass per level

exams.name: Celpe-Bras
exams.format: Task-based, no separate discrete-skill sections
exams.scoring: Intermediate to Advanced Superior certificate levels

zh.name: Mandarin Chinese
zh.framework: own scale, mapped to CEFR informally

exams.name: HSK (Levels 1-9, 2021 standard)
exams.body: Center for Language Education and Cooperation (China)
exams.format: Level-specific fixed exams
exams.scoring: Pass threshold ~60%, per level

exams.name: HSKK (Speaking)
exams.body: Center for Language Education and Cooperation (China)
exams.format: Beginner/Intermediate/Advanced oral exam, separate from HSK
exams.scoring: 0-100 scaled score

exams.name: JLPT (N5-N1)
exams.body: Japan Foundation / Japan Educational Exchanges and Services
exams.format: No speaking or writing production section — this is a real gap you can fill
exams.scoring: Pass thresholds vary by level, section minimums apply

exams.name: TOPIK I (1-2) / TOPIK II (3-6)
exams.body: National Institute for International Education, South Korea
exams.format: No speaking section in the standard TOPIK; separate speaking test (TOPIK Speaking) launched more recently
exams.scoring: Pass thresholds by level, TOPIK II scored 0-300 combined

exams.name: TORFL / TRKI
exams.body: Russian Ministry of Education certified centers
exams.format: Level-specific (Elementary through IV), used for study/work visas
exams.scoring: Pass per subtest

ar.name: Arabic
ar.framework: no single dominant global exam; fragmented by institution

exams.name: Arabic Language Proficiency Test (varies by university, e.g. King Saud University, Qatar's Arabic-CEFR project)
exams.body: Institution-dependent — no single global Arabic exam has the market position IELTS/HSK/DELF have
exams.format: Not standardized across institutions
exams.scoring: Not standardized — flag for manual research per target market

hi.name: Hindi
hi.framework: no single globally dominant standardized exam

exams.name: Central Institute of Hindi various proficiency diplomas
exams.body: Central Institute of Hindi, India (under Ministry of Education)
exams.format: Regional/institutional, not globally standardized like DELF/HSK
exams.scoring: Not standardized — flag for manual research

content_build_instructions: For each exam, pull the CURRENT official specimen paper / handbook from the exam body's own site before writing mock-test content — formats and scoring change over exam cycles.

Languages without a standardized global exam (Arabic, Hindi, and most under-resourced languages) should ship with a strong CEFR-style proficiency ladder + institution-specific prep modules added opportunistically, rather than waiting for a single 'IELTS equivalent' that doesn't exist.

JLPT and the standard TOPIK have no (or limited) speaking/writing production sections — this is a genuine product opportunity: Sparky can offer speaking/writing practice that these official exams don't test but that real fluency requires, marketed honestly as 'beyond the exam' rather than 'exam-identical'.
